newsitem.title: USA: California unveils $6.1 billion housing program.
newsitem.headline: California unveils $6.1 billion housing program.

text.p: California unveiled Thursday a $6.1 billion plan that will provide tens of thousands of home loans and build apartments for low-income families across the state.
Republican Gov. Pete Wilson said the five-year business plan -- adopted by the California Housing Finance Agency -- would fund loans for an estimated 51,500 affordable homes and apartment units.
"This plan will also mean new jobs in the construction industry and building trade," Wilson said in a statement.
The state estimated that the new construction activity under the program would create nearly 70,000 jobs.
The housing agency provides low interest mortgage loans to first-time homebuyers. The agency also funds construction of rental apartments for low-income families.

To help fund the five-year program, the agency was expected to issue more than $4 billion of bonds. The program will not cost the state money because mortgage payments by homebuyers should generate enough revenues to repay the bonds, the agency said.
